messages:
alex (platform): Heads-up — legal wants a per-route "who changed what" card on the console + an NDJSON export for audits. Need guidance on minimal export shape and what we surface in-UI.
priya (product): Agreement from compliance. They need the ability to filter by route, actor, time-range, and rollout id. Also want to see effective quota/limit values at the time of change.
ben (security): Must include actor provenance and a pseudonymized id. We shouldn't export cleartext emails for bulk exports. Suggest `actor_id_hash` + `actor_role`. Also include `reason` when present.
jamie (console): UX question: for big policy diffs (JSON blobs) do we show a compact diff + "view full"? Collapsed summary could be "+3 rules, 2 weight changes" with expand.
maya (infra): For export shape, proposing NDJSON lines; example below for one change event:
```
{"ts":"2026-03-18T15:02:31Z","route":"/v1/generate","change_type":"update","actor_id_hash":"sha256:abcd...","actor_role":"engineer","before":{"quota":1000,"policy":"round_robin"},"after":{"quota":1500,"policy":"weighted:0.7/0.3"},"justification":"increase for marketing campaign","rollout_id":"rollout_2026_0318_01","redaction_mode":"pseudonymize"}
```
ben (security): That looks okay. Add `actor_ip_redacted` boolean and `pii_masking_level` (none/partial/full) so consumers know how to interpret rows.
priya (product): UI should show a header with Who / When / Action / Rollout / Delta. Clicking Delta expands to a side panel with before/after + small diff visualization.
alex (platform): On the API side: we need a compact query param `since_ts` and `route=` + `redaction=` for on-the-fly exports. Example CLI: `redwood audit export --route /v1/generate --since 2026-03-01 --redaction pseudonymize > out.ndjson`
jamie (console): We'll add an inline badge on route detail: "last config change 2h ago by priya (product)" and a link "View changelog" that opens the NDJSON preview + download button. :link: 
ben (security): Also require `signed_export` option for enterprise customers (server signs bundle with KMS key). Otherwise we risk tampering.
maya (infra): Implementation note: keeping a canonical precomputed `effective_snapshot` per change will make UI fast. We can store small diffs + cached snapshot for last N changes. Storage cost negligible compared to query load.
priya (product): Edge case: what if change happened during a multi-step rollout? Need `rollout_phase` (`canary`, `ramped`, `rolled_back`) and `percentage` if applicable.
alex (platform): Good call. Add `rollout_phase` + `rollout_percentage`. Also include `deployment_id` when change originated from infra auto-deploy.
auditbot: Note — export request received: job_id=job_9876 status=queued (:+1:).
jamie (console): For the diff visual, let's show inline highlights for added/removed keys and a tiny sparkline for quota over time. Keeps it scannable.
ben (security): Don't forget retention policy metadata: `retention_policy` and `deleted_at` (null if active). Must be present for compliance.
maya (infra): We'll expose a new internal API `GET /internal/v1/audit/ndjson` that accepts `route, since_ts, redaction, signed` and streams NDJSON. Can wire RBAC to dedicated export role.
priya (product): Action items: 1) Define final NDJSON schema in spec doc, 2) Jamie to mock UI, 3) Maya + Alex to prototype internal API, 4) Ben to sign off on redaction/pseudonymization.
alex (platform): I'll open an RFC issue with the proposed schema and link tickets. Assigning prototypes to maya/jamie.
ben (security): Quick question: do we allow producers to request `full_identity` exports for legal with extra approval? If so we need audit trail of that approval.
priya (product): Yes — `full_identity` only via signed PO + manual approval flow. We record `approval_id` and `approver` in each exported row when full_identity is enabled.
alex (platform): Cool. If no objections I'll draft the RFC today.
jamie (console): No objections from me. Will start mocks tomorrow.
ben (security): 👍
maya (infra): 👍
alex (platform): thanks all — filing RFC: https://r.redwood/rfcs/459 (placeholder).
